{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wi-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"06029fca3092685174548a6e114b596ad92645f0f242dd6af0b1fd7b3f701f62","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wi-class-d:lineage:23","source_registry_sha256":"9dcfc0d0c3044debd01d4cb03103f48fb860797364a23b2cb56d36c868619a64","source_liveness_sha256":"4ca51030ff51b3372629ada1c05ad91f501dabccdcf7931dab678c717e7bb9b6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Signals, pavement markings and lane controls: traffic lights and arrows, white and yellow lines, crosswalks and special lanes","heading":"C — Signals, pavement markings and lane controls: red, yellow and green lights and arrows, edge and lane lines, crosswalks, yellow passing lines, shared center, reversible, reserved and flex lanes","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Signals, pavement markings and lane controls: red, yellow and green lights and arrows, edge and lane lines, crosswalks, yellow passing lines, shared center, reversible, reserved and flex lanes
Knowledge domain: what each traffic light, arrow and pavement line tells you to do, and how Wisconsin's special lanes are used — core rules-of-the-road material for the knowledge test.

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
Traffic signals usually stand at intersections and stack red on top, yellow in the middle and green at the bottom. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
Many intersections out in the country have only a single yellow or red light. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
If a traffic light has no power or is not working properly, treat the intersection as if it had a stop sign. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
When a police officer is directing traffic at a signal, follow the officer's directions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
At a steady red light, stop completely and wait until the light turns green and cross traffic has cleared. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
You may turn right on a steady red when it is safe and no sign forbids the turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A01
A left turn on red is allowed only when you are turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A01
Any turn on red starts with a full stop; then yield to all traffic and complete the turn staying in your lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A01
At a flashing red light, stop completely and then go when it is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A01
At a steady red arrow, stop completely and wait for the light to turn green. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A01
At a flashing red arrow, stop completely and then go when it is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A02
A steady yellow light means red is coming, so slow down and stop before you enter the intersection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A02
If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, do not stop; keep going through. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A02
At a flashing yellow light, slow down, look for cross traffic and go ahead with caution. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A02
A steady yellow arrow means the arrow is about to turn red, and you should stop if you can do so safely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A02
At a flashing yellow arrow, yield before making the turn and then proceed with caution. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A02
A steady green light lets you go through the intersection, but you must still yield to emergency vehicles and others the law requires. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A02
If you were stopped and the light turns green, let cross traffic clear the intersection before you go. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A02
On a steady green you may turn left only when it is safe, because oncoming traffic has the right-of-way. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A02
A steady green arrow lets you turn the way it points with no oncoming or crossing traffic expected, but you still watch for pedestrians. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A03
Lines and symbols on the pavement divide the road into lanes, show where passing and lane changes are allowed and which lanes are for turns, and their color tells you whether the road is one-way or two-way. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A03
A solid white line marks the right edge of the travel lane, and a solid or dashed yellow line marks the left edge of the lanes going your way. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A03
White dashed lines separate lanes going the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe, and a white pavement arrow shows the direction that lane must go. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A03
A solid white line between lanes may not be crossed except to avoid a hazard or when you are turning within the next block. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A03
At a crosswalk, stop with your front wheels just short of the solid white line and never stop on the crosswalk itself. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A03
Crosswalks are usually at intersections but sometimes sit in the middle of a block, and pedestrians there may have their own signals. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A04
Solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and two solid yellow lines mean neither direction may pass. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A04
You may cross a double solid yellow line to turn into a driveway when it is safe. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A04
You may also cross it to pass a vehicle moving at less than half the speed limit when safe, but not if that vehicle is farm equipment. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A04
A dashed yellow line means you may pass when it is safe, while watching for other traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A04
Where a dashed yellow line runs beside a solid one, only drivers on the dashed side may pass. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A04
Some passing zones also have signs showing where passing is and is not allowed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-F33 | anchor: A05
A shared center lane is only for left turns and U-turns, can be used by traffic from either direction, and is marked with white left-turn arrows. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F34 | anchor: A05
You may cross the solid yellow line into a shared center lane to make a left turn or U-turn, but only enter it when it is safe. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F35 | anchor: A05
Reversible lanes run on different hours for each lane, are marked with double dashed yellow lines, and use special overhead lights to show which lanes you may use. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F36 | anchor: A05
Over a reversible lane, a red X means the lane is closed, a green arrow means it is open, and a yellow X means it is changing, so move into a lane with a green arrow. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F37 | anchor: A06
Reserved lanes are only for the type of vehicle named on the sign, are often marked with a white diamond on the sign and pavement, and are illegal to use in any other vehicle. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F38 | anchor: A06
You may drive in a reserved lane to turn across it within the next half of a block, and if a bicyclist is in it, move in behind them and turn when safe. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F39 | anchor: A06
Signs for bus and car pool lanes may list the days and hours when the restriction applies. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F40 | anchor: A06
Bus and bike lanes may be painted in colors such as red, green or gray; follow the pavement lettering and posted signs. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F41 | anchor: A07
On some highways signs allow the paved shoulder to be used as a flex lane, which is separated by a solid yellow line and opened according to traffic volume and special events. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F42 | anchor: A07
Large trucks may not drive in a flex lane. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F43 | anchor: A07
If there is an incident along a flex lane, yellow and red X signals tell drivers to merge into the next lane. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F44 | anchor: A07
Over a flex lane, a green arrow means open, a yellow X means it is closing so merge into the general-purpose lanes, and a red X means closed. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F45 | anchor: A07
A Merge sign marks the end of the flex lane, where you merge back into the general-purpose lanes. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0042]

Misconceptions: a dark or broken signal is not a free-for-all, it is treated as a stop sign; a green light does not mean go immediately if cross traffic is still clearing; you do not slam on the brakes when the light turns yellow after you are already in the intersection; left on red is not legal from a two-way street; the slow-vehicle passing exception never covers farm equipment.
Mnemonics: flashing red means stop then go, steady red means stop and wait; white lines split lanes going your way, yellow lines split you from oncoming traffic; dashed means you may, solid means you may not; red X closed, yellow X leave, green arrow drive.
Glossary: steady signal means a light that stays on; flashing signal means a light that blinks on and off; edge line means the line marking the side of the travel lane; shared center lane means a middle lane for left turns from both directions; reversible lane means a lane whose direction changes by time of day; reserved lane means a lane for one vehicle type such as buses or bikes; flex lane means a shoulder opened as a travel lane.
Dynamic facts: reversible, reserved and flex lanes open and close by posted hours, traffic volume and special events, so read the lane lights and signs each time you drive them.
